name: Institute of Machine Learning and Neural Computation – Maass group (Wolfgang Maass)
topics: successor representations;synaptic plasticity;cognitive maps;goal-directed planning;spiking networks
summary: Models how biological neural circuits and plasticity rules such as behavioral time-scale plasticity can implement successor-relation based reinforcement learning and goal-directed planning.
question: How do plasticity rules in biological neural networks support learning of cognitive maps and goal-directed decisions?

name: Trusted AI Group (Bettina Könighofer)
summary: Combines formal verification, reactive synthesis and machine learning to build shields and runtime enforcement that keep reinforcement learning agents safe.
question: How can formal methods provide safety guarantees for learning-enabled autonomous systems?

name: Chatterjee Group (Krishnendu Chatterjee)
institution: Institute of Science and Technology Austria
topics: rl with reachability objectives;pac guarantees;stochastic games;formal verification;game theory
summary: Studies reinforcement learning with formally specified objectives such as reachability, with PAC and optimality guarantees in MDPs and stochastic games.
question: What guarantees can learning algorithms provide for formally specified objectives in stochastic systems and games?

name: Institute for Machine Learning (Sepp Hochreiter)
topics: reward redistribution;credit assignment;recurrent action models;offline rl;rl for reasoning models
summary: Works on reward redistribution for credit assignment, extending the RUDDER line to reasoning models, and on recurrent xLSTM-based large action models trained offline.
question: How can rewards be redistributed and sequence models built so that agents assign credit efficiently over long horizons?

name: Autonomous Systems Lab (Dongheui Lee)
topics: real-world rl;legged locomotion;contact-rich manipulation;learning from demonstration
summary: Develops robot learning methods, including real-world RL for contact-rich manipulation and RL with model-based supervision for torque-controlled locomotion.
question: How can robots acquire new motor skills autonomously, building on observation of human behaviour?

name: Cyber-Physical Systems Research Unit – Grosu group (Radu Grosu)
topics: real-time recurrent rl;neural circuit policies;liquid networks;autonomous driving;mean-field rl
summary: Develops biologically inspired recurrent policies and real-time recurrent RL for online adaptation of pretrained controllers, with applications in autonomous driving.
question: How can compact, biologically inspired neural controllers learn and adapt online in partially observable control tasks?

name: Trustworthy Cyber-Physical Systems group (Ezio Bartocci)
summary: Studies the specification, verification and interpretation of RL policies, including rule-based explanations of continuous-action policies.
question: How can RL policies used in cyber-physical systems be specified, verified and explained?

name: Quantum Information & Computation Group (Hans J. Briegel)
topics: projective simulation;interpretable rl;collective behaviour;artificial agency;physics-inspired learning
summary: Develops projective simulation, a physics-inspired model of learning agents, and uses RL agents to study agency and emergent collective behaviour.
question: How can physical models of learning explain and implement agency in artificial agents?

name: Data Mining and Machine Learning group (Sebastian Tschiatschek)
summary: Studies optimization and representation problems in deep RL, such as plasticity loss and hyperbolic representations, and rule-guided policy evaluation and improvement.
question: Why does training of deep RL agents become unstable or lose plasticity, and how can it be made reliable?

name: Holroyd lab – cognitive control and reward (Clay Holroyd)
topics: reward prediction error;anterior cingulate cortex;hierarchical behavior;eeg
summary: Studies neural reward signals such as the reward positivity and the role of anterior cingulate cortex in reward-driven, hierarchically organized behavior.
question: How does the brain use reward signals to learn and control hierarchically organized behavior?

name: Verguts lab – computational cognitive neuroscience (Tom Verguts)
summary: Builds computational models of how humans adapt learning rates, explore and control behavior in changing environments.
question: How do humans adapt their learning and control strategies to the structure of their environment?

name: IDLab – AI for energy (Chris Develder)
topics: energy systems;ev charging;battery control;model predictive control;interpretable rl
summary: Applies RL, often combined with model predictive control, to demand response, battery and EV charging control in power systems.
question: How can learning-based control manage flexible energy assets in power systems efficiently and reliably?

name: IDLab – Simoens group (Pieter Simoens)
summary: Studies RL agents through the lens of cognitive science, including interval timing, policy compression and inverse RL for alignment.
question: Which cognitive mechanisms, such as timing and resource limits, can make RL agents behave more like humans and animals?

name: Ernst group – RL and energy (Damien Ernst)
topics: asymmetric actor-critic;partial observability;world models;exploration;energy and plasma control
summary: Develops RL for partially observable control, including asymmetric actor-critic methods and world models, with energy, wind-farm and plasma applications.
question: How can RL solve complex decision and control problems, especially in energy systems?

name: Machine Learning Group – Lenaerts (Tom Lenaerts)
summary: Studies cooperation in multi-agent RL, including task generation that requires cooperation and the role of unrewarded subgoals.
question: How do cooperation and collective behavior emerge and get learned in groups of agents?

name: Artificial Intelligence Lab Brussels – RL (Ann Nowé; Diederik M. Roijers)
topics: multi-objective rl;multi-agent rl;explainable rl;policy distillation;continual learning
summary: Works on multi-agent and multi-objective RL and on distilling deep RL policies into interpretable models.
question: How can RL agents handle multiple objectives and multiple agents while remaining interpretable?

name: INSAIT 3D vision group (Danda Pani Paudel)
topics: agentic rl;diffusion policy optimization;3d scene generation;vision-language models
summary: Applies reinforcement learning to vision tasks, including agentic RL for controllable 3D scene generation and policy optimization of diffusion models.
question: How can RL-trained agents and models generate and reason about 3D scenes from vision and language?

name: Milan Češka
summary: Uses deep reinforcement learning together with formal synthesis to compute finite-state controllers for (hidden-model) POMDPs.
question: How can deep RL scale the synthesis of robust controllers for partially observable systems?

name: Game Theory group, AI Center (Viliam Lisý)
summary: Develops reinforcement learning and search algorithms for zero-sum imperfect-information games, including learned world models and test-time adaptation.
question: How can agents learn models and reason with them to play well in large imperfect-information games?

name: LiVe Lab – Learning in Verification (Jan Křetínský)
topics: ltl-guided rl;robustness certification;stochastic games;probabilistic model checking;safe rl
summary: Combines machine learning and verification, including multi-task RL from LTL instructions, robustness certification of RL policies and risk-aware decision-making.
question: How can learning and formal verification be combined to obtain controllers that are both efficient and trustworthy?

name: Kim G. Larsen (Aalborg, DEIS)
summary: Larsen's group combines model checking and strategy synthesis with reinforcement learning, building shields that keep learning agents safe.
question: How can verification and synthesis produce safe, secure and optimal strategies for cyber-physical systems, including learned ones?

name: Sebastian Risi group (Sebastian Risi)
summary: Risi's group studies neuroevolution, self-organising and open-ended systems, including evolutionary approaches to continual reinforcement learning.
question: Can we create lifelong learning machines that continuously acquire new knowledge and skills?

name: Aalto Robot Learning (Joni Pajarinen)
summary: The lab works on reinforcement learning for robots, including exploration, multi-objective and offline meta-RL, and decision making under partial observability.
question: How can autonomous robots learn to accomplish complex tasks in unstructured environments?

name: Computational Behavior Lab (Antti Oulasvirta)
topics: computational rationality;rl models of users;rlhf;human-computer interaction;user simulation
summary: The lab builds computational-rationality models of human behaviour, often trained with reinforcement learning, and applies them to interactive systems and RL from human feedback.
question: How can computational models of human behaviour, built on bounded optimal decision making, be used to design interactive and intelligent systems?

name: Intelligent Robotics group (Ville Kyrki)
summary: The group develops learning methods for robots in unstructured environments, including reinforcement and imitation learning for manipulation, co-design and driving.
question: How can robots learn to operate reliably in unstructured environments built for humans?

name: Gilles Stoltz (online learning and bandits)
summary: Works on online learning and contextual bandits, including RL-based expert policy orchestration.
question: How can sequential prediction and decision methods stay robust when data are adversarial or non-stationary?

name: CREST-ENSAE – Perchet (Vianney Perchet)
summary: Works on the theory of bandits, online learning and RL, including RL with transition lookahead and learning in markets.
question: What are the optimal ways to learn and decide online when feedback is partial and strategic?

name: Criteo AI Lab – sequential decision making (Marc Abeille)
summary: Industry research on bandit and RL theory, including exploration in linear bandits and learning in contextual and lookahead MDPs.
question: How can online systems explore efficiently with provable guarantees?

name: Aurélien Garivier (bandit theory)
summary: Works on the statistics of sequential decision making, including best-arm and best-transition identification and risk-sensitive planning.
question: What are the optimal sample complexities of identification and planning problems in sequential decision making?

name: Eric Moulines (RL and stochastic approximation theory)
summary: Proves convergence and sample-complexity results for policy gradient, actor-critic and Q-learning methods via stochastic approximation.
question: What finite-sample guarantees can be proven for RL algorithms built on stochastic approximation?

name: Huawei Noah's Ark Lab Paris (Balázs Kégl)
summary: Industry research on decentralized hierarchical multi-agent RL and on reward-based training objectives for generative models.
question: How can learning agents be organized hierarchically to control complex systems?

name: Human Reinforcement Learning team (Stefano Palminteri)
summary: Characterizes the computational processes and biases of human RL, such as relative value encoding and asymmetric learning rates.
question: Which computational processes and biases govern how humans learn from rewards and punishments?

name: Supaero Reinforcement Learning Initiative – SuReLI (Emmanuel Rachelson)
topics: combinatorial optimization;branch and bound;model-based rl;world models
summary: Studies RL and sequential decision problems, including model-based RL for exact combinatorial optimization.
question: How do learning and optimization mechanisms work in sequential decision problems, and how can they be improved?

name: Inria Flowers (Pierre-Yves Oudeyer; Clément Moulin-Frier)
summary: Studies curiosity-driven, autotelic RL agents that set their own goals, including LLM-based agents and artificial societies.
question: Which mechanisms enable open-ended, curiosity-driven learning and development in humans and machines?

name: Inria Thoth – Gaillard (Pierre Gaillard)
summary: Works on online learning theory, including reset-free online MDPs, convex RL and multinomial logistic MDPs.
question: Which regret guarantees can online learning methods achieve in sequential decision problems?

name: Inria POLARIS (Nicolas Gast; Bruno Gaujal)
summary: Develops learning and control for large stochastic systems, including restless bandits, Whittle indices and regret in average-reward MDPs.
question: How can mean-field and stochastic models give efficient, provable learning algorithms for large Markov decision processes?

name: Inria Scool (Philippe Preux; Odalric-Ambrym Maillard; Emilie Kaufmann; Riad Akrour)
lead: Philippe Preux; Odalric-Ambrym Maillard; Emilie Kaufmann; Riad Akrour
institution: Inria Lille / Université de Lille / CNRS
topics: bandits;best arm identification;exploration;interpretable rl;applied sequential decision making
summary: Studies sequential decision making under uncertainty through bandit and RL problems, from theory to applications in health, agriculture and ecology.
question: How should an agent make sequential decisions under uncertainty, and with what guarantees?

name: Inria Argo – Bušić (Ana Bušić)
topics: multi-agent rl;delayed rl;wind farm control;learning in games
summary: Studies optimization, control and learning for energy networks, including delayed cooperative multi-agent RL and wind farm control benchmarks.
question: How can learning-based control coordinate many agents in energy networks with renewables?

name: Inria Sierra – Bach (Francis Bach)
summary: Contributes optimization and learning theory to RL post-training of language models, including RLHF alignment collapse and advantage weighting.
question: Which optimization principles explain the behavior of RL post-training for large models?

name: Inria Willow (Justin Carpentier)
summary: Develops RL methods that exploit physics and differentiable simulation, including survival-based goal-conditioned RL and Sobolev RL.
question: How can robots reason about and act in the physical world by combining physics-based models with learning?

name: Inria NEO – Avrachenkov (Konstantin Avrachenkov)
summary: Studies the structure of optimal policies in MDPs and POMDPs and learning in restless bandits.
question: Which structural properties of stochastic decision problems make optimal policies efficient to learn and compute?

name: LAAS-CNRS Gepetto (Nicolas Mansard)
summary: Combines trajectory optimization and differentiable models with RL to control humanoid and legged robots.
question: How can anthropomorphic robots generate and control complex movement, using both optimal control and learning?

name: Meta FAIR Paris – Behavioural foundation models / zero-shot RL (Alessandro Lazaric)
primary: zero-shot rl and behavioural foundation models
topics: zero-shot rl;forward-backward representations;humanoid control;world models;unsupervised rl
summary: Builds behavioural foundation models pre-trained without task rewards, such as Meta Motivo for humanoid control, and studies representations and jumpy world models for zero-shot RL and planning.
question: Can a single behavioural foundation model, pre-trained without rewards, solve new control tasks zero-shot at inference time?

name: Meta FAIR Paris – Rémi Munos
summary: Works on RL theory and on RL methods for language-model reasoning, such as trained search policies that steer exploration and RL-based post-training for Lean theorem proving.
question: Can exploration in language-model reasoning be steered by learned search policies instead of naive repeated sampling?

name: Naver Labs Europe – Spatial AI (Christian Wolf)
summary: Industry research on embodied agents trained with RL for visual and social navigation, including memory architectures.
question: How can robots learn high-level reasoning and navigation skills from visual observations?

name: Motivation, Brain and Behaviour team – MBB (Mathias Pessiglione)
summary: Studies how the brain represents costs and benefits in decisions, including computational models of reward learning in patients and drug effects.
question: How are costs and benefits represented in the brain, and how is this trade-off biased by emotion, fatigue and disease?

name: ISIR MLIA – Thome (Nicolas Thome)
summary: Works on sample-efficient model-based RL on real robots and on vision-language reward models and world models for embodied agents.
question: How can embodied agents learn useful world models and rewards from limited interaction?

name: ISIR – RL and developmental robotics (Olivier Sigaud; Nicolas Perrin-Gilbert; Stéphane Doncieux)
lead: Olivier Sigaud; Nicolas Perrin-Gilbert; Stéphane Doncieux
topics: goal-conditioned rl;behavioral foundation models;quality diversity;offline rl;robot learning
summary: Develops goal-conditioned, zero-shot and quality-diversity RL methods for robots and open-ended agents.
question: How can robots acquire diverse, reusable skills through reinforcement learning and exploration?

name: ISIR – decision making in robots and animals (Mehdi Khamassi)
summary: Models decision making and RL in animals and robots, including model arbitration, curiosity-driven exploration and hippocampal replay.
question: How do animals and robots combine learning, reward and curiosity to make decisions?

name: LIRIS – Matignon (Laëtitia Matignon)
summary: Works on deep multi-agent RL, exploration and transfer with behavioral foundation models, and socially compliant robot navigation.
question: How can multiple learning agents coordinate and transfer what they have learned?

name: Sylvain Lamprier (robust and offline RL)
summary: Works on robust, offline and exploration-driven deep RL, including style-aligned offline RL and reward-preserving attacks.
question: How can deep RL agents learn diverse, robust behaviors from limited or adversarial data?

name: Triesch Lab (Jochen Triesch)
summary: The lab models brain development and builds developmental AI agents that learn autonomously, using intrinsic rewards and deep reinforcement learning.
question: How can artificial agents learn completely autonomously, like infants and children, by exploring and interacting with the world?

name: Quantum Computing group, Fraunhofer IKS (Jeanette Miriam Lorenz)
summary: Benchmarks and implements quantum reinforcement learning algorithms, including single-file reference implementations.
question: How can quantum reinforcement learning be benchmarked fairly against classical methods?

name: Pattern Recognition Lab (Andreas Maier)
summary: Applies deep and offline reinforcement learning to decision problems such as distribution-grid protection and trade execution.
question: How can deep RL be applied reliably to control and decision problems in energy systems and finance?

name: Helmholtz Institute for Human-Centered AI (Eric Schulz)
summary: Studies exploration and learning from interaction in humans and machine agents, including the theory of goal-conditioned RL and skill learning.
question: What computational principles govern how humans and machines explore and learn from interaction?

name: Adaptive Generalist Learning Lab (André Biedenkapp)
summary: The group develops contextual reinforcement learning methods for adaptable, generalist policies and applies RL to dynamic algorithm configuration.
question: How can giving RL agents contextual information about their environment make policies generalise when conditions change?

name: Autonomous Learning Robots Lab – ALR (Gerhard Neumann)
topics: episodic rl;maximum-entropy rl;diffusion policies;off-policy actor-critic;movement primitives
summary: The lab develops machine learning methods for robotics, including episodic and off-policy reinforcement learning, diffusion-based maximum-entropy RL and imitation learning.
question: Which machine learning methods let robots learn versatile skills efficiently from interaction and demonstrations?

name: Applied Technical-Cognitive Systems (J. Marius Zöllner)
institution: Karlsruhe Institute of Technology / FZI Research Center for Information Technology
summary: The group works on perception and behaviour decision for autonomous vehicles and robots, including distributional and expert-guided reinforcement learning for safe driving.
question: How can technical-cognitive systems such as autonomous vehicles understand situations and decide on behaviour reliably?

name: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Chair (Eyke Hüllermeier)
summary: The chair works on preference-based reinforcement learning and RL from human feedback, reward modelling and multi-task bandits.
question: How can learning systems use preference feedback and quantified uncertainty to learn reliably, for example in RL from human feedback?

name: Mobile and Distributed Systems Group (Claudia Linnhoff-Popien)
summary: Studies multi-agent reinforcement learning, including peer incentivization for cooperation and interpretable RL, alongside quantum computing methods.
question: How can autonomous systems be built with methods from AI and quantum computing?

name: Spatial AI group (Matthias Schubert)
primary: RL for mobility and resource allocation
summary: Applies reinforcement learning, including offline RL with diffusion world models, to mobility and resource-allocation tasks.
question: How can RL agents be trained to optimize mobility and resource-allocation decisions?

name: Tresp Lab (Volker Tresp)
summary: Develops reinforcement learning methods for language-model agents, such as RL-trained memory management and efficient rollout reuse.
question: How can reinforcement learning give language-model agents better memory, reasoning and tool use?

name: AutoML / AutoRL group (Marius Lindauer)
summary: The group applies AutoML methods to reinforcement learning (AutoRL), studying hyperparameter optimisation, network growth and generalisation of RL agents.
question: How can automating the design decisions in the RL pipeline make reinforcement learning sample-efficient, stable and broadly applicable?

name: Department of Computational Neuroscience (Peter Dayan)
institution: Max Planck Institute for Biological Cybernetics
topics: neural rl;neuromodulation;model-based and model-free control;decision-making;computational psychiatry
summary: The department builds and tests computational models of how humans and animals learn to choose actions from rewards and punishments, including neuromodulation and neural reinforcement learning.
question: How do humans and other animals come to choose appropriate, and sometimes inappropriate, actions in the face of rewards and punishments?

name: Learning and Dynamical Systems Group (Michael Muehlebach)
institution: Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems
topics: model-based rl;partially observable rl;learning control;online optimization;robotics
summary: The group combines machine learning, dynamical systems and control theory, including model-based and partially observable reinforcement learning for robot control.
question: How can a-priori known structure of physical systems make learning-based control more sample-efficient and generalisable?

name: Machine Teaching Group (Adish Singla)
institution: Max Planck Institute for Software Systems
summary: The group studies machine teaching, including curriculum design for RL agents, policy teaching and RL from human feedback, with applications in education.
question: How can AI systems teach and be taught effectively, for example through curriculum design for learning agents?

name: Multi-Agent Systems Group (Goran Radanovic)
institution: Max Planck Institute for Software Systems
summary: The group studies the robustness and accountability of reinforcement learning, including corruption-robust offline RL and distributionally robust RL from human feedback.
question: How should AI systems with multiple, possibly self-interested agents be designed and analysed to be robust and accountable?

name: Marquardt Division (Florian Marquardt)
institution: Max Planck Institute for the Science of Light
topics: quantum control;quantum circuit design;model-based rl;scientific discovery
summary: Uses reinforcement learning to discover control strategies and circuits for quantum devices, as part of work on machine learning for physics.
question: Can machine learning act like a scientist and discover new strategies for controlling quantum devices?

name: Data Science in Mechanical Engineering – DSME (Sebastian Trimpe)
summary: The institute develops learning and control algorithms for physical machines, including safe and model-based reinforcement learning.
question: How can robots and other physical machines learn from limited real-world data while keeping guarantees on safety and performance?

name: Artificial Intelligence and Formal Methods – AI-FM (Nils Jansen)
summary: The group combines reinforcement learning with formal verification, working on shielded safe RL and policies for partially observable and uncertain models.
question: How can machine learning be combined with formal verification to give AI systems that are safe, robust and dependable?

name: Computational Neuroscience Group (Sen Cheng)
primary: rl models of memory and navigation
summary: The group builds deep reinforcement learning and neural network models of hippocampal memory and spatial navigation and compares them with animal and human data.
question: How do episodic memory and hippocampal processes support learning and spatial navigation, as seen through reinforcement learning agents?

name: Learning Technical Systems (Setareh Maghsudi)
topics: multi-armed bandits;multi-agent rl;online learning;decision-making under uncertainty;networked systems
summary: The chair studies decision-making under uncertainty with bandit algorithms and multi-agent reinforcement learning for networked engineering systems.
question: How can networked multi-agent systems make good decisions under uncertainty in engineering settings such as IoT and energy management?

name: Theory of Machine Learning / Optimization of Adaptive Systems (Tobias Glasmachers)
primary: structured deep rl and industrial rl
summary: The group adds structure to deep reinforcement learning for navigation and industrial control and combines RL with evolutionary optimisation.
question: How can deep reinforcement learning systems be given additional structure to become truly autonomous, e.g. for efficient navigation and object-oriented actions?

name: Foundations of Artificial Intelligence – FAI (Jörg Hoffmann)
summary: The group combines AI planning with learned action policies, working on testing, verification and safe training of reinforcement-learned policies.
question: How can action policies learned by reinforcement learning be tested and verified so they are safe to use in planning problems?

name: Learning and Intelligent Systems Lab (Marc Toussaint)
topics: task and motion planning;robot manipulation;reinforcement learning;curriculum learning;physical reasoning
summary: The lab bridges AI reasoning, optimisation and machine learning for robotics, including combining constrained sampling-based planning with reinforcement learning for manipulation.
question: How does the interplay of learning and reasoning, of data-based and model-based decision making, yield strongly generalising robot intelligence?

name: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Lab (Kristian Kersting)
summary: The lab works on neurosymbolic and interpretable deep reinforcement learning, such as pretraining with logical options and evaluating RL agents against human-level generalisation.
question: How can statistical learning and symbolic reasoning be combined so that agents understand complex worlds and act responsibly?

name: Human and Machine Cognition Lab (Charley Wu)
summary: The lab uses reinforcement-learning-inspired computational models and behavioural experiments to study how humans explore, learn and use social information.
question: How do people make efficient use of limited cognitive resources to explore and learn, including from other people, and what can machine learning take from this?

name: IKIDA – Interactive AI Algorithms and Cognitive Models (Dorothea Koert)
topics: interactive rl;human advice;multi-agent coexistence;human-robot interaction;policy blending
summary: The group studies interactive reinforcement learning with human input and policy blending for multi-agent coexistence in human-robot settings.
question: How can robots learn interactively from human input while handling unreliable advice and coexisting with other agents?

name: Intelligent Autonomous Systems Lab (Jan Peters)
summary: The lab develops reinforcement learning, policy search and imitation learning methods for robot motor skills, manipulation and control on real hardware.
question: How can robots learn motor and manipulation skills from interaction that are fast, stable and reliable enough for real hardware?

name: Interactive Robot Perception & Learning Lab – PEARL (Georgia Chalvatzaki)
topics: mobile manipulation;maximum-entropy rl;diffusion policies;bimanual manipulation;embodied ai
summary: The lab studies robot learning for mobile manipulation, including diffusion-based maximum-entropy reinforcement learning and RL-driven data generation for bimanual dexterous manipulation.
question: How can robots acquire mobile manipulation skills through purposeful interaction so they can assist people in everyday tasks?

name: Psychology of Information Processing Lab (Constantin Rothkopf)
topics: inverse rl;human decision-making;active vision;agent evaluation;bayesian models
summary: The lab models human perception, decision-making and action with inverse reinforcement learning and Bayesian methods and compares deep RL agents with human behaviour.
question: How do humans use perception actively during extended natural behaviour to form beliefs and guide goal-directed decisions and actions?

name: Self-Organizing Systems Lab (Heinz Koeppl)
summary: The lab studies large ensembles of interacting agents and uses mean-field reinforcement learning and control for large-scale multi-agent problems.
question: How can large ensembles of reconfigurable agents collectively solve complex tasks such as self-assembly, distributed sensing and control?

name: Applied and Theoretical Aspects of Robot Intelligence Lab (Majid Khadiv)
topics: humanoid control;rl tracking policies;trajectory optimization;legged locomotion;sim-to-real
summary: Combines optimal control and machine learning for legged and humanoid robots, generating motions with trajectory optimization and transferring them to hardware through RL tracking policies.
question: How can robots autonomously plan in new situations and continually improve their skills in the real world?

name: Chair of Information-oriented Control (Sandra Hirche)
summary: Develops data-driven and learning-based control with formal guarantees, including continuous-time offline RL and safe exploration via bandits.
question: How can data-driven and learning-based control come with guarantees under uncertainty and limited data?

name: Chair of Robotics, Artificial Intelligence and Real-time Systems (Alois Knoll)
summary: Studies lifelong and meta-reinforcement learning for robots, including preserving and reusing knowledge across tasks and skill priors for long-horizon manipulation.
question: How can robots preserve and combine knowledge across tasks so that they keep acquiring new skills?

name: Cyber-Physical Systems Group (Matthias Althoff)
topics: safe rl;action projection;reachability analysis;verifiably robust rl;rl for control
summary: Develops provably safe reinforcement learning that combines set-based reachability analysis with action projection and shielding, applied to autonomous vehicles, robots and power systems.
question: How can learning-based controllers be provably guaranteed to operate safely in uncertain environments?

name: Learning Systems and Robotics Lab (Angela Schoellig)
topics: safe rl;safety filters;learning-based control;aerial robotics;differentiable simulation
summary: Combines control, machine learning and optimization for safe learning-based robot control, including safety-filtered RL and GPU-accelerated drone simulators for policy learning.
question: How can robots in unstructured, changing environments learn while keeping guarantees on safety, performance and reliability?

name: Reinforcement Learning Group Dresden (Ostap Okhrin)
summary: The group applies deep reinforcement learning to autonomous driving and vessels, including safe RL for rare-event risk control in urban driving.
question: How can reinforcement learning make autonomous vehicles and vessels in transport safer and more efficient?

name: Autonomous Intelligent Systems (Sven Behnke)
summary: The group builds cognitive robots and uses reinforcement learning and latent world-model planning for manipulation and humanoid control.
question: How can cognitive robots act competently in complex, uncertain real-world environments?

name: Humanoid Robots Lab (Maren Bennewitz)
topics: constrained rl;multi-objective rl;robot navigation;autonomous driving;agricultural robotics
summary: The lab develops perception, planning and learning methods for robots, including constraint-aware and multi-objective reinforcement learning.
question: How can robots perceive, plan and act autonomously in cluttered and dynamic real-world environments?

name: Biological Psychology Lab (Jan Peters, Cologne)
summary: The lab studies human reinforcement learning and exploration with computational models, pharmacology and neuroimaging, including model-based control in gambling disorder and RNN agents.
question: How do dopamine and related mechanisms shape exploration and model-based versus model-free control in human decision-making?

name: Neurorobotics Lab (Joschka Boedecker)
summary: The lab develops data-efficient deep reinforcement learning methods built on Q-learning for robotics, autonomous driving and neurotechnology.
question: How can deep reinforcement learning give robust, sample-efficient and adaptive decision policies for real-world robots and devices?

name: Robot Learning Lab (Abhinav Valada)
summary: The lab works on robot learning for mobility and manipulation, including RL fine-tuning of diffusion policies inside learned world models and self-play driving policies.
question: How can robot learning algorithms for mobility and manipulation reach autonomy at scale?

name: Knowledge Technology (Stefan Wermter)
summary: The group develops neuroscience-inspired learning agents and robots, including RL from AI feedback and agentic skill discovery with reinforcement learning.
question: How can nature-inspired hybrid neural and symbolic representations yield continually learning robots and agents with vision and language?

name: Latent Learning Lab (Nicolas W. Schuck)
topics: neural replay;state representations;latent cause inference;decision-making;computational psychiatry
summary: The lab combines behavioural and neuroimaging studies with reinforcement-learning-inspired models to study how the brain forms task state representations and uses replay for learning and decisions.
question: How does the brain build the representation of the current task state that reinforcement learning needs, and how does replay shape it?

name: Technical Aspects of Multimodal Systems – TAMS (Jianwei Zhang)
topics: curriculum rl;humanoid loco-manipulation;world models;table tennis;robot learning
summary: The group develops robot learning methods, including curriculum reinforcement learning for agile skills and RL-based whole-body control for humanoids.
question: How can multimodal robots learn agile and compositional skills, such as humanoid loco-manipulation, from interaction?

name: Applied Probability / RL Theory Group (Leif Döring)
topics: policy gradient;q-learning theory;convergence analysis;stochastic optimization;dynamic programming
summary: The group studies the mathematics of reinforcement learning, including convergence of policy gradient methods and the role of target networks in Q-learning.
question: What rigorous insight into the stochastic foundations of reinforcement learning can bring algorithmic improvements?

name: Learning and Interactive Robots – LaIR (Jens Kober)
summary: Develops RL and interactive imitation learning for robot motor skills, including guided exploration and hierarchical RL.
question: How can robots learn motor skills efficiently from their own experience and from human feedback?

name: Machine Learning and Positioning Systems Lab (Christopher Mutschler)
topics: safe rl;constrained rl;successor representations;risk-aware exploration;interpretable rl
summary: Develops constrained and risk-aware reinforcement learning methods with safety and stability guarantees aimed at deployment in safety-critical systems.
question: How can reinforcement learning be made safe, stable and explainable enough for safety-critical deployment?

name: Vernade Lab (Claire Vernade)
summary: Studies the theory of sequential decision-making, including bandit algorithms with complex or delayed feedback and lifelong and meta-reinforcement learning.
question: What principles allow interactive learning systems to adapt reliably as their tasks and feedback change?

name: Autonomous Learning / Distributed Intelligence Group (Georg Martius)
summary: The group studies autonomous learning in embodied agents through intrinsically motivated, model-based and constrained reinforcement learning for robot control.
question: How can an embodied agent decide what to learn, how to learn it and how to judge its own learning success?

name: Autonomous Vision Group (Andreas Geiger)
summary: The group works on perception and sensorimotor control for autonomous systems, including reinforcement learning of driving planning policies with simple rewards and RL post-training in simulation.
question: How can autonomous systems such as self-driving cars become more autonomous, efficient, robust and safe?

name: Neuro-Cognitive Modeling Group (Martin V. Butz)
topics: contextual rl;event-predictive models;causal discovery;active inference;cognitive modeling
summary: The group develops event-predictive cognitive models and contextual reinforcement learning methods, including framing causal discovery as an RL problem.
question: How does the brain learn and maintain context-conditioned, event-predictive structures that generate and control attention, thought and behaviour?

name: Intelligent Space and Energy Systems (Günther Waxenegger-Wilfing)
summary: Studies reinforcement learning and planning for autonomous decision-making in safety-critical, data-scarce space and propulsion applications.
question: How can sequential decision-making algorithms let AI systems act autonomously and reliably in safety-critical, data-scarce environments?

name: Reinforcement Learning and Computational Decision-Making (Carlo D'Eramo)
topics: value-based rl;multi-agent rl;multi-task rl;curriculum learning;transfer learning
summary: Develops methods that make deep RL more efficient and practical, including stable value estimation, multi-agent policy gradients, and transfer, curriculum and multi-task learning.
question: How can reinforcement learning be made efficient and practical enough for challenging real-world decision-making and control?

name: Reinforcement Learning and Computational Decision-Making (Carlo D'Eramo)
topics: value-based rl;temporal-difference learning;multi-task rl;curriculum rl;multi-agent rl
summary: The group develops methods to make reinforcement learning more efficient and practical, including temporal-difference learning, transfer, curriculum, multi-task and multi-agent RL.
question: How can reinforcement learning be made efficient and practical enough for challenging real-world decision-making and control problems?

name: Vesoma (Martin Riedmiller)
topics: humanoid control;data-efficient rl;learning from interaction;vla fine-tuning
summary: Humanoid-robot start-up registered in December 2025 whose AI research, led by Martin Riedmiller, aims at robots that learn tasks through their own real-world interaction.
question: How can humanoid robots become self-improving agents that learn new tasks from their own interaction with the world?

name: Computational Intelligence and Deep Learning group – CIDL (Anastasios Tefas)
primary: deep rl for robotics and trading
topics: deep rl;robust rl;robot perception;financial trading;uav localization
summary: The group develops deep reinforcement-learning methods for robotics, UAV localisation and financial trading, with a focus on robustness and data efficiency.
question: How can computational intelligence and deep learning give robots and other agents robust perception and decision making?

name: Intelligent Systems Lab (Ioannis Vlahavas)
summary: The lab applies deep reinforcement learning to autonomous driving, driver-assistance systems and game agents alongside AI planning research.
question: How can AI planning and learning techniques solve complex decision problems such as autonomous driving?

name: Ivana Dusparic (Trinity College Dublin)
topics: multi-objective rl;traffic control;model-based rl;constrained rl;autonomous systems
summary: Dusparic's group develops reinforcement-learning methods, including multi-objective, constrained and model-based RL, for traffic control and other large-scale urban infrastructures.
question: How can AI, especially reinforcement learning, optimise resources in large-scale urban infrastructures such as transport systems?

name: Human-Robot Interfaces and Interaction Lab – HRI² (Arash Ajoudani)
topics: safe rl;contact-rich manipulation;non-prehensile manipulation;quadruped locomotion;human-robot interaction
summary: The lab works on physical human-robot interaction and uses safe and sim-to-real reinforcement learning for contact-rich manipulation and legged locomotion.
question: How can robots physically interact and collaborate with humans safely and adaptively?

name: Nicola Gatti (Politecnico di Milano)
primary: online learning in games and markets
summary: Gatti works at the intersection of game theory and learning, proving regret guarantees for constrained MDPs, bandits and online learning in economic settings.
question: How can online learning minimise regret in equilibrium and economic problems such as auctions and constrained decision processes?

name: Real Life Reinforcement Learning Lab – RL3 (Marcello Restelli)
summary: The group develops reinforcement-learning algorithms with theoretical guarantees, including policy-gradient, imitation and inverse RL methods, and applies them to domains such as energy, finance and robotics.
question: How can reinforcement-learning algorithms be designed for complex environments while keeping both theoretical guarantees and real-world applicability?

name: Cognitive Cooperating Robots Lab (Luca Iocchi)
topics: non-markovian rewards;model-based rl;multi-uav rl;cognitive robotics;reward machines
summary: The lab works on cognitive robotics and includes reinforcement learning with non-Markovian rewards and multi-agent RL for robots and UAVs.
question: How can cognitive robots combine reasoning and learning, including learning from non-Markovian rewards, to act and cooperate?

name: Network Control Laboratory (Francesco Delli Priscoli)
summary: The lab applies deep and multi-agent reinforcement learning to control problems such as vehicle platooning, insulin dosing, medical imaging and space debris capture.
question: How can multi-agent learning techniques control and manage complex networked systems in health, energy, transport and communications?

name: Laboratory for Artificial Intelligence and Learning Algorithms – LAILA (Nicolò Cesa-Bianchi)
topics: multi-armed bandits;online learning;partial monitoring;delayed feedback;multi-agent learning
summary: The lab studies the foundations of learning algorithms, proving regret bounds for bandits, online learning and reinforcement-learning settings with delayed or partial feedback.
question: What are the foundations of learning algorithms for sequential decision making, from online learning and bandits to reinforcement learning?

name: Automation and Robotics Research Group (Holger Voos)
primary: rl for aerial and space robots
topics: goal-conditioned rl;uav control;space robotics;model predictive control
summary: Applies RL, sometimes combined with MPC, to the control of UAVs, manipulators and space robots.
question: How can learning-based control make aerial, space and manipulator robots act autonomously in uncertain conditions?

name: Space Robotics group – SpaceR (Miguel Olivares-Mendez)
summary: Trains RL controllers and benchmarks for spacecraft docking, inspection, planetary robots and fault-tolerant control.
question: How can robots learn to operate autonomously in space and planetary environments?

name: CWI Machine Learning group – Koolen (Wouter M. Koolen)
topics: best arm identification;multi-objective bandits;online learning;game tree search
summary: Works on the theory of pure exploration in multi-armed bandits and related online learning problems.
question: What are the fundamental limits of pure exploration in bandit models, and which algorithms reach them?

name: Autonomous Multi-Robots Lab (Javier Alonso-Mora)
summary: Develops planning and learning methods for teams of mobile robots, including multi-agent RL for cooperative aerial manipulation.
question: How can teams of autonomous robots navigate, coordinate and act safely in dynamic environments shared with humans?

name: Böhmer Research Lab (Wendelin Böhmer)
summary: Studies why deep RL agents fail to generalize out of distribution and develops offline, model-based and tree-search methods that transfer better.
question: Which structural choices let deep RL agents generalize beyond the situations they were trained on?

name: Della Santina group – soft robot learning (Cosimo Della Santina)
summary: Combines models of soft and compliant robots with RL to learn locomotion, jumping and whole-arm manipulation that exploits body dynamics.
question: How can robots use the physical intelligence of soft and compliant bodies, together with learning, to act in the real world?

name: Interactive Intelligence – multi-objective and inverse RL (Luciano Cavalcante Siebert; Pradeep K. Murukannaiah)
lead: Luciano Cavalcante Siebert; Pradeep K. Murukannaiah
summary: Uses multi-objective and inverse RL to represent human values and intentions in autonomous systems, with applications such as water management and climate policy.
question: How can autonomous systems account for human values and intentions when they learn to act?

name: Interactive Learning and Decision Making (Frans Oliehoek)
summary: Works on decision making for agents that interact with complex worlds and other agents, including multi-agent RL, partially observable RL and game-theoretic learning.
question: How can an agent learn and decide well when it interacts with a complex world that includes other agents?

name: Micro Air Vehicle Lab – MAVLab (Guido de Croon)
topics: drone racing;model-based rl;sim-to-real;vision-based control;micro air vehicles
summary: Trains end-to-end and model-based RL controllers for small drones, including vision-based racing and sim-to-real transfer of depth perception.
question: How can tiny drones fly autonomously with very limited onboard sensing and computation?

name: Sequential Decision Making group – Spaan lab (Matthijs Spaan)
topics: bayesian rl;epistemic uncertainty;planning with mcts;safe rl;pomdps
summary: Studies uncertainty-aware and Bayesian deep RL, safe exploration and search-based planning for agents acting under partial observability.
question: How can agents plan and learn good policies over time when their models of the world are uncertain?

name: AI for decision-making – Information Systems group (Yingqian Zhang; Hendrik Baier)
summary: Applies deep and programmatic RL to scheduling, routing and other combinatorial optimization problems in logistics and manufacturing.
question: How can data-driven decision-making methods such as deep RL solve operational optimization problems reliably and interpretably?

name: Data and AI cluster – Pechenizkiy group (Mykola Pechenizkiy)
topics: safe rl;continual rl;multi-agent rl;benchmarks;unsupervised skill discovery
summary: Builds benchmarks and methods for safe, continual and multi-agent RL, alongside work on trustworthy machine learning.
question: How can learning systems, including RL agents, be made robust, safe and trustworthy?

name: Thiago D. Simão (safe RL)
summary: Develops safe RL algorithms and GPU-accelerated benchmarks for settings with constrained interaction with an unknown environment.
question: How can agents learn good behavior in unknown environments while respecting safety constraints during learning?

name: Reinforcement Learning Group Leiden (Thomas Moerland; Aske Plaat)
topics: model-based rl;safe rl;zero-shot rl;policy mirror descent;rl for llm agents
summary: Researches the combination of planning and learning in RL, plus safe RL, zero-shot RL and RL for language-model agents.
question: How can planning and learning be combined so that agents learn through trial and error more effectively?

name: Department of Advanced Computing Sciences – game AI and RL (Dennis Soemers; Kurt Driessens)
lead: Dennis J. N. J. Soemers; Kurt Driessens
summary: Combines RL and search for game-playing agents, including self-play with non-neural learners and action-duration learning.
question: How can reinforcement learning and search be combined to build general game-playing agents?

name: Microsoft Research AI for Science – Elise van der Pol
summary: Studies symmetry and structure in deep RL, including expected-return symmetries for coordination and group-structured world models.
question: How can symmetry and structure make deep RL more efficient and useful for science?

name: Artificial Cognitive Systems Lab (Marcel van Gerven)
summary: Connects learning, inference and control in natural and artificial systems, including reward-modulated learning rules and recurrent RL policies.
question: Which computational mechanisms support learning, inference and control in natural and artificial systems?

name: Amsterdam Machine Learning Lab – van Hoof group (Herke van Hoof)
summary: Studies data-efficient RL, including replay correction, task composition and policies that generalize across instructions and tasks.
question: How can RL agents learn efficiently by reusing structure across tasks?

name: Prosocial Dynamics Lab (Fernando P. Santos)
summary: Models populations of adaptive and RL agents to study cooperation and fairness, with applications to transport network design.
question: How do behavioral dynamics in systems of adaptive learning agents shape cooperation and fairness, and how can such systems be designed to be prosocial?

name: Sabatelli group (Matthia Sabatelli)
summary: Studies the learning dynamics of deep RL agents, including plasticity loss, double descent and low-dimensional representations.
question: What happens inside deep RL networks during training, and how can that knowledge make agents learn more reliably?

name: Wouter van Heeswijk (RL for operations)
summary: Applies RL to operations research and finance problems, including large discrete and hybrid action spaces.
question: How can RL handle the large, structured action spaces of real operations and financial decision problems?

name: Intelligent Systems – multi-agent RL (Shihan Wang; Mehdi Dastani)
summary: Studies multi-agent deep RL, including communication, credit assignment, exploration and symbolic action masking.
question: How can complex agent-agent and human-agent interactions be modelled and integrated into reinforcement learning?

name: Vincent François-Lavet group (Vincent François-Lavet)
topics: representation learning;model-based rl;generalization;rl for llms;energy applications
summary: Studies deep RL agents that generalize from limited data, with a focus on representation learning, world models and applications such as energy trading.
question: How can agents learn sequential decision-making tasks while generalizing from limited data?

name: Anastasios Lekkas (NTNU Engineering Cybernetics)
institution: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)
topics: deep rl;marine vehicles;dynamic positioning;explainable ai;guidance and control
summary: Lekkas's group applies deep reinforcement learning and explainable AI to guidance, navigation and control of surface and underwater vessels, including field trials.
question: How can AI methods such as reinforcement learning be merged with control engineering to give marine cyber-physical systems more autonomy?

name: Autonomous Robots Lab (Kostas Alexis)
institution: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)
summary: The lab develops resilient autonomous robots and uses deep reinforcement learning for navigation, active perception and legged locomotion.
question: How can autonomous robots operate resiliently over long periods in complex and degraded environments?

name: Sébastien Gros (NTNU Engineering Cybernetics)
institution: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)
topics: safe rl;model predictive control;data-driven control;energy systems;mpc-based policies
summary: Gros's group combines reinforcement learning with model predictive control to obtain safe, data-driven controllers for energy, process and vehicle systems.
question: How can reinforcement learning and model predictive control be combined into safe, data-driven controllers?

name: Robotics and Intelligent Systems group – ROBIN (Jim Tørresen)
topics: deep rl;multi-robot navigation;bio-inspired computing;llm-guided rl;adaptive robots
summary: Tørresen's group works on bio-inspired and adaptive robotics, including deep reinforcement learning for multi-robot navigation and LLM-assisted decision making.
question: How can bio-inspired computing and machine learning make robots adapt in complex real-world settings?

name: Rafał Kucharski lab (Rafał Kucharski)
summary: Uses multi-agent reinforcement learning to study how autonomous vehicles' collective behaviour affects urban traffic, and how agents cooperate with changing partners.
question: How will autonomous vehicles trained with reinforcement learning change urban traffic dynamics?

name: Marek Cygan
topics: value function scaling;multi-task rl;reward-conditioned rl;continuous control;robot manipulation
summary: Works on scaling and regularizing value functions for sample-efficient and multi-task continuous-control RL, with links to robotic manipulation.
question: How can value-based RL scale model capacity to become compute- and sample-efficient across many tasks?

name: Piotr Miłoś group (Piotr Miłoś)
summary: Studies off-policy and continual deep RL, including replay, overestimation and plasticity in actor-critic methods, and learned representations for planning.
question: Which methods can deliver robust decision-making in complex scenarios?

name: Computer Vision Lab – RL team (Tomasz Trzciński; Michał Bortkiewicz)
summary: Studies self-supervised and contrastive goal-conditioned RL, including scaling network depth and learning representations of action sequences.
question: Can scaling self-supervised RL unlock new goal-reaching capabilities?

name: Paton Lab (Joseph Paton)
summary: The lab records and manipulates neural activity in behaving rodents to study how dopamine and basal-ganglia circuits implement temporal-difference and distributional learning of future reward over time.
question: How do animals learn which cues predict behaviourally important events, treating credit assignment as inference in the time domain?

name: AI for People and Society group – Francisco S. Melo (INESC-ID)
topics: multi-agent rl;ad hoc teamwork;risk-aware mdps;inverse rl;planning
summary: Melo's group develops reinforcement-learning and decision-theoretic planning methods for agents that interact with other agents, including ad hoc teamwork, value-decomposition MARL and risk-aware MDPs.
question: How can autonomous agents learn and plan to interact with other agents, human or artificial, in complex and possibly unknown environments?

name: Multiagent Systems group – value-aligned RL (Juan A. Rodríguez-Aguilar)
topics: multi-agent rl;value alignment;multi-objective rl;ethical environment design;norms
summary: The group designs multi-agent reinforcement-learning environments and multi-objective RL methods that provably incentivise agents to behave in line with ethical values.
question: How can multi-agent systems, including learning agents, be built to act in line with the ethical and social values of the people who use them?

name: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning group (Anders Jonsson)
summary: The group studies sequential decision problems for one or several agents, combining reinforcement learning with automated planning and hierarchical problem structure.
question: How can agents find and exploit structure, hierarchy and planning to solve single- and multi-agent sequential decision problems efficiently?

name: Gergely Neu (UPF)
summary: Neu works on the theory of sequential decision making, proving regret and sample-complexity guarantees for reinforcement learning, bandit and online-optimization algorithms.
question: What are provably efficient algorithms and fundamental limits for sequential decision making in online optimization, bandits and reinforcement learning?

name: Theoretical and Cognitive Neuroscience lab (Rubén Moreno-Bote)
summary: The lab combines computational and cognitive neuroscience to study how brains decide and learn from reward, and contributes to reinforcement-learning methods such as successor features.
question: What computational principles let brains perceive, decide and learn from reward, and how can they inform learning agents?

name: Karinne Ramirez-Amaro (Chalmers)
topics: hierarchical rl;symbolic planning;skill chaining;vlm rewards;robot manipulation
summary: Ramirez-Amaro's group combines symbolic models and planning with hierarchical reinforcement learning for long-horizon robot manipulation.
question: How can symbolic knowledge and planning make robot reinforcement learning work on long-horizon, multi-skill tasks?

name: Alexandre Proutiere (KTH Decision and Control Systems)
summary: Proutiere works on statistically optimal algorithms for bandits and reinforcement learning, including low-rank and hierarchical zero-shot RL and diffusion-based model-based RL.
question: What are the statistically optimal ways to learn and control in reinforcement-learning and bandit problems, and how do they apply to networked systems?

name: Jana Tumova (KTH RPL)
topics: temporal logic;multi-agent rl;causal rl;safe planning;formal methods
summary: Tumova combines formal methods and temporal-logic specifications with planning and learning, including multi-agent and causal reinforcement learning for robots and vehicles.
question: How can formal specifications such as temporal logic guide safe planning, control and learning for robots and multi-agent systems?

name: Karl H. Johansson (KTH Decision and Control Systems)
topics: inverse rl;bandit optimization;platoon control;networked control;cyber-physical systems
summary: Johansson's group works on networked and distributed control and includes reinforcement-learning, inverse-RL and bandit-optimisation methods for vehicles and networked systems.
question: How can networked and distributed cyber-physical systems be controlled and estimated reliably, including through learning?

name: Robotics, Perception and Learning Lab (Danica Kragic)
topics: robot manipulation;preference-based rl;safe rl;diffusion policies;visuomotor learning
summary: The lab works on robot manipulation and learning, including preference-based and safe reinforcement learning and visuomotor diffusion policies.
question: How can robots combine perception and machine learning to act and manipulate in the physical world?

name: Disney Research – Robotics, Zurich (Moritz Bächer)
summary: Trains expressive locomotion, motion-tracking and falling policies with deep RL for legged and animated robotic characters using GPU simulation.
question: How can RL bring animated characters to life as physical robots with stylized yet robust motion?

name: Adaptive Systems Laboratory (Ali H. Sayed)
topics: multi-agent rl;policy optimization;partial observability;distributed learning;social learning
summary: Analyses adaptation and learning over networks of agents, including multi-agent policy optimization and RL under partial observability.
question: How can networks of adaptive agents with learning abilities cooperate and learn in uncertain environments?

name: Biorobotics Laboratory – BioRob (Auke Ijspeert)
summary: Studies animal locomotion control with robots and neuromechanical simulation, and uses RL for whole-body control of salamander-like and legged robots.
question: What neural mechanisms underlie movement control and learning in animals, and how can they inspire robot control?

name: CLAIRE (Caglar Gulcehre)
summary: Works on sample-efficient and offline RL and on RL-based alignment and algorithm discovery with large language models.
question: How can learning algorithms make efficient and safe use of experiential data and weak, sparse or noisy feedback?

name: Chair of Business Analytics – BAN (Negar Kiyavash)
summary: Studies causal and contextual bandits and RL from combined reward and preference feedback, grounded in causal inference.
question: How can causal structure be inferred and exploited for efficient sequential decision-making?

name: Computational Robot Design & Fabrication Lab – CREATE (Josie Hughes)
summary: Builds tendon-driven and swimming robots and studies sim-to-real transfer of RL policies through better physical models and system identification.
question: How can robots be designed and used differently, with data-driven design and large-scale physical experimentation?

name: Computer Vision Laboratory – CVLab (Pascal Fua)
summary: Computer vision lab that also develops on-policy RL with expert guidance and preference optimization for physically plausible humanoid motion.
question: How can machines interpret images and recover 3D shape and motion, and use them for physically grounded control?

name: Data Science & AI Lab – dlab (Robert West)
summary: Develops RL-with-verifiable-rewards methods for language-model reasoning alongside work on NLP and AI safety.
question: How can AI systems be built that are safe for humanity, at the intersection of AI, NLP and computational social science?

name: Dependable Control and Decision Group – DECODE (Giancarlo Ferrari-Trecate)
topics: neural control;stability guarantees;policy parametrization;safe rl;distributionally robust control
summary: Develops policy parametrizations and learning methods for neural controllers with built-in stability guarantees, including stability-constrained RL.
question: How can learning-based controllers become more autonomous and self-adapting while remaining dependable?

name: Information and Network Dynamics Lab – INDY (Matthias Grossglauser)
summary: Develops hierarchical and causal RL and dueling-bandit methods that combine reward and preference feedback.
question: How can large dynamical systems involving human and technical agents be modelled and controlled from data?

name: Laboratory for Information and Inference Systems – LIONS (Volkan Cevher)
topics: imitation learning;rl theory;preference optimization;multi-agent learning;minimax optimization
summary: Develops provably efficient algorithms for imitation learning, value-based RL, preference-based alignment and multi-agent learning.
question: How can mathematical theory and computational methods learn efficiently from incomplete data, including interaction, demonstrations and preferences?

name: Laboratory of Computational Neuroscience (Wulfram Gerstner)
topics: three-factor learning rules;novelty and surprise;exploration;synaptic plasticity;computational neuroscience
summary: Models how reward, novelty and surprise act as third factors in synaptic plasticity and drive exploration in humans and neural networks.
question: How do neuromodulatory signals such as reward, novelty and surprise gate learning in neural circuits?

name: Mathis Group (Alexander Mathis)
topics: musculoskeletal control;motor learning;motion imitation;embodied ai;computational neuroscience
summary: Uses deep RL and imitation learning to train controllers for musculoskeletal models of human and animal bodies and relates them to motor neuroscience.
question: How do brains acquire adaptive motor skills, and can RL agents controlling realistic musculoskeletal bodies help explain this?

name: Risk Analytics and Optimization Chair (Daniel Kuhn)
summary: Develops distributionally robust optimization methods for dynamic decision problems, including robust Markov decision processes and bandits.
question: How can large-scale dynamic decision problems under uncertainty be modelled and solved reliably?

name: SYCAMORE – Systems Control and Multiagent Optimization Research (Maryam Kamgarpour)
summary: Develops theory for multi-agent RL, inverse RL and constrained or safe RL, building on game theory and stochastic control.
question: How can multiple agents make good decisions in uncertain and dynamic environments?

name: Visual Intelligence for Transportation – VITA (Alexandre Alahi)
topics: social navigation;safe rl;world models;autonomous driving;agentic workflows
summary: Applies RL and world models to safe social navigation and autonomous mobility, and RL to the training of LLM meta-agents.
question: How can machines interpret and anticipate human behaviour to move safely and efficiently among people?

name: Computational Robotics Lab (Stelian Coros)
summary: Studies computational design and control of robots, including RL with simulation-to-real transfer and online fine-tuning on physical hardware.
question: How should future robots be made and controlled so they can operate in complex environments and interact with people?

name: Dörfler Group, Automatic Control Laboratory (Florian Dörfler)
topics: policy gradient;adaptive control;data-driven control;linear-quadratic control;rl and control
summary: Studies policy-gradient and data-driven methods for adaptive control of unknown or time-varying dynamical systems, connecting RL and control theory.
question: How can data-driven and policy-gradient methods control unknown dynamical systems with guarantees?

name: Edge AI & Intelligence Sensing Lab, Project-Based Learning Center (Michele Magno)
summary: Develops RL controllers that train or run on resource-constrained embedded platforms such as scaled autonomous race cars and small quadrupeds.
question: How can energy-efficient edge intelligence let embedded robots learn and act on board?

name: Intelligent Control Systems Group (Melanie Zeilinger)
topics: safe rl;model predictive control;learning-based control;exploration;safety filters
summary: Combines model predictive control with learning, including RL and online model learning, to obtain controllers with safety guarantees for uncertain systems.
question: How can high-performance learning-based control be made safe for systems that act in uncertain environments and interact with humans?

name: Language, Reasoning and Education Lab (Mrinmaya Sachan)
primary: rl for llm reasoning and tutoring
topics: rl for llms;multi-turn rl;pedagogical alignment;llm reasoning;intelligent tutoring
summary: Uses RL, including multi-turn RL, to train language models for reasoning and to align them with pedagogical goals in tutoring.
question: How can language models reason reliably and be aligned to teach well rather than only solve problems?

name: Learning & Adaptive Systems Group (Andreas Krause)
summary: Develops RL and sequential decision-making methods that use uncertainty estimates for safe exploration, model-based control and data-efficient learning on real robots.
question: How can learning systems actively acquire information, reason and make reliable decisions in complex, uncertain domains?

name: Lygeros Group, Automatic Control Laboratory (John Lygeros)
topics: markov decision processes;dynamic programming;risk-averse control;deep rl applications;stochastic control
summary: Develops large-scale solvers and theory for Markov decision processes, including risk-averse MDPs, and applies deep RL to scheduling problems.
question: How can large-scale and risk-averse sequential decision problems be solved efficiently and reliably?

name: Optimization & Decision Intelligence Group (Niao He)
summary: Analyses RL, constrained exploration, RLHF and learning in mean-field games through optimization and learning theory.
question: How can optimization and learning theory yield provably efficient and trustworthy automated decision-making?

name: Robotic Systems Lab (Marco Hutter)
summary: Trains locomotion and manipulation controllers for legged robots and construction machines with simulation-based deep RL and learned world models, deployed on hardware.
question: How can new control and learning algorithms give legged robots dynamic, versatile locomotion and manipulation in the real world?

name: Rycolab (Ryan Cotterell)
topics: rl for llms;process reward models;kl regularization;llm reasoning
summary: NLP lab whose RL work covers RL post-training with search-informed process rewards and KL-divergence estimation for RLHF.
question: How can formal and statistical methods improve the training and reasoning of language models?

name: Soft Robotics Lab (Robert Katzschmann)
primary: rl for dexterous and soft robots
summary: Applies offline and real-world RL to dexterous robot hands and to bio-inspired soft and underwater robots.
question: How can robots built from soft, rigid and living materials learn adaptive interactions with their environments?

name: Zenke Lab (Friedemann Zenke)
institution: Friedrich Miescher Institute for Biomedical Research
summary: Computational neuroscience lab that develops reconstruction-free world models for model-based RL and planning alongside work on biologically plausible learning.
question: How do neural circuits learn predictive representations of the world that support planning and control?

name: Google – Paradigms of Intelligence team, Zurich (João Sacramento)
topics: hierarchical rl;temporal abstraction;multi-agent cooperation;in-context learning;learning awareness
summary: Studies how sequence models trained with RL can explore through temporally abstract internal actions and reach cooperation among self-interested learning agents by in-context inference about co-players.
question: How can the in-context learning of sequence models support hierarchical exploration and cooperation among learning agents?

name: Swiss AI Lab IDSIA – Schmidhuber Group (Jürgen Schmidhuber)
summary: Works on upside-down RL, curiosity-driven agents, world models and policy optimization, with group members affiliated with IDSIA and KAUST.
question: How can an AI system improve itself through curiosity-driven exploration, world models and learning to learn?

name: Sony AI – Zurich (Peter Dürr)
topics: model-free rl;robot table tennis;sim-to-real;event-based vision;optimal control
summary: Builds real-time robot systems trained with model-free RL, including a table-tennis robot competitive with elite players, and links RL to optimal control.
question: How can RL control physical robots in fast, adversarial real-time interaction such as table tennis?

name: Bogunovic Group (Ilija Bogunovic)
topics: bandits;rl for llms;world models;robust optimization;preference alignment
summary: Develops bandit, Bayesian optimization and RL methods that are robust to uncertainty, applied to LLM reasoning, alignment and world-model learning.
question: How can sequential decision-making remain reliable under uncertainty and adversarial conditions, from bandits to training large models?

name: Lucchi Group (Aurelien Lucchi)
summary: Studies RL-based post-training of language models for reasoning, including curricula at the edge of model capability and multi-task GRPO.
question: How can optimization and RL post-training make language-model reasoning reliable across tasks?

name: Rhine AI Lab (Ilija Bogunovic)
primary: RL for LLMs and robust decision making
topics: rl post-training;world-model learning;bayesian optimisation;robust learning;llm alignment
summary: Develops RL and bandit methods for language-model post-training, regret-driven world-model learning and robust sequential decision making.
question: How can learning agents make sample-efficient and robust sequential decisions, from bandits to RL post-training of language models?

name: Dimitrakakis Group (Christos Dimitrakakis)
summary: Studies Bayesian and inverse RL, bandit learning in games and matching markets, and fairness and privacy in sequential decision-making.
question: How can agents make approximately optimal sequential decisions under uncertainty while respecting constraints such as fairness and privacy?

name: Ramponi Group (Giorgia Ramponi)
summary: Studies the theory and algorithms of inverse RL, imitation and preference-based RL, and multi-agent learning.
question: How can agents learn objectives and policies from demonstrations and preferences, alone and in multi-agent settings?

name: Robotics and Perception Group (Davide Scaramuzza)
summary: Trains quadrotor controllers with model-free, model-based and multi-agent RL for agile vision-based flight and drone racing, transferred from simulation to real drones.
question: How can autonomous drones navigate using only onboard cameras and computation, without external infrastructure?

name: Songbird Group, Institute of Neuroinformatics (Richard Hahnloser)
institution: University of Zurich and ETH Zurich
topics: vocal learning;motor exploration;basal ganglia;zebra finch;rl theory
summary: Studies how zebra finches learn song and analyses their learning strategies and motor exploration with RL theory.
question: Which reinforcement-learning strategies do songbirds use to learn their songs, and how does the avian brain implement them?

name: Graph Machine Learning Group (Cesare Alippi)
topics: multi-agent rl;graph neural networks;continual rl;non-stationary environments
summary: Develops graph-based multi-agent RL methods, including message-passing policies and continual learning in non-stationary environments.
question: How can learning systems operate on graph-structured, non-stationary dynamical systems, including multi-agent RL?

name: Google DeepMind – AlphaProof / RL for formal mathematics (Thomas Hubert)
summary: Develops AlphaProof, an AlphaZero-style RL and search system that proves olympiad-level mathematics in the Lean formal language, and follow-up proof-search systems for research mathematics.
question: Can reinforcement learning with formal verification reach and extend expert-level mathematical reasoning?

name: Google DeepMind – André Barreto
topics: successor features;transfer in rl;reward modelling;agency;diverse behaviour
summary: Studies how RL problems can be decomposed into simpler tasks whose solutions are recombined, along with work on reward uncertainty, agency and plasticity in RL agents.
question: How can reinforcement learning problems be decomposed into simpler tasks whose solutions combine to solve the original problem quickly?

name: Google DeepMind – Hado van Hasselt
topics: policy optimisation;meta-learned rl algorithms;value-based rl;off-policy learning
summary: Works on core deep RL algorithms, including Wasserstein policy optimisation and RL update rules discovered by meta-learning.
question: Can better reinforcement learning update rules be designed, or discovered automatically from the experience of many agents?

name: Google DeepMind – Robotics and control (Nicolas Heess; Abbas Abdolmaleki)
summary: Develops RL and self-improvement methods for continuous control and robot manipulation, including value learning from observation data and RL-style fine-tuning of vision-language-action policies.
question: How can robot policies keep improving from their own experience and unlabelled data instead of relying only on demonstrations?

name: Google DeepMind – Will Dabney
topics: distributional rl;on-policy rl;experience replay;dopamine and value coding;agency
summary: Works on distributional and deep RL methods and on links between RL and neuroscience, including distributional value coding in the brain.
question: What are the missing ingredients on the path from current deep RL agents to human-level learning, and what can the brain's value coding tell us about them?

name: Adaptive & Intelligent Robotics Lab – AIRL (Antoine Cully)
topics: quality-diversity;evolutionary rl;open-ended skill discovery;curriculum learning;robot adaptation
summary: Develops quality-diversity and evolutionary RL algorithms that let robots discover diverse skills and adapt to new situations.
question: How can physical robots autonomously adapt to new and unforeseen situations, such as a new environment, task or damage?

name: Alessandra Russo (Imperial College London)
topics: neuro-symbolic rl;reward machines;skill transfer;unsupervised environment design
summary: Develops neuro-symbolic and logic-based methods for RL, including learned task structures, skill transfer and environment design.
question: How can symbolic and neuro-symbolic learning make agents robust, interpretable and explainable?

name: Francesco Belardinelli (Imperial College London)
summary: Develops shielding and other formal-methods techniques for safe single- and multi-agent RL.
question: How can formal methods make reinforcement learning and multi-agent systems safe?

name: Robot Learning Lab (Edward Johns)
summary: Develops imitation and RL methods for robot manipulation, including large-scale simulated RL from generated object models.
question: How can robots learn manipulation skills efficiently and generally enough to assist in everyday environments?

name: Safe Whole-body Intelligent Robotics Lab – SWIRL (Stephen James)
topics: online rl;offline rl;imitation learning;world models;robot benchmarks
summary: Works at the intersection of online RL, offline RL and imitation learning for robots, including humanoid manipulation benchmarks.
question: How can robots learn safely and sample-efficiently using their entire physical embodiment?

name: Ineffable Intelligence (David Silver)
topics: learning from experience;self-play;superhuman agents;rl without human data
summary: Start-up David Silver founded after leaving Google DeepMind (announced January 2026) to build RL systems that learn from their own experience rather than from human data.
question: Can a learning system discover knowledge and skills entirely from its own experience, without human data?

name: Carmine Ventre (King's College London)
topics: market making;multi-agent rl;algorithmic trading;rl environments;game theory
summary: Applies single- and multi-agent RL to market making and trading, including model-based simulation environments.
question: How can RL agents for algorithmic trading and market making be designed and evaluated?

name: Cooperative AI Lab (Yali Du)
topics: cooperative marl;safe marl;human-ai coordination;continual marl;value alignment
summary: Develops scalable multi-agent RL, safe hierarchical MARL and human-AI coordination methods.
