question: How can cooperative and safe AI agents learn, coordinate and align with humans in complex decision-making environments?

name: Matteo Leonetti (King's College London)
topics: hierarchical rl;abstraction;ad hoc teamwork;planning and learning;robotics
summary: Works on hierarchical RL with abstractions and on combining RL with planning for autonomous robots and teamwork.
question: How can reinforcement learning be combined with planning and reasoning for autonomous robots?

name: Zeb Kurth-Nelson (Max Planck UCL Centre)
institution: Max Planck UCL Centre for Computational Psychiatry and Ageing Research, University College London
primary: replay and RL in the brain
topics: neural replay;deep rl models of the brain;distributional coding;credit assignment
summary: Studies neural replay, credit assignment and distributional reward coding in humans using models inspired by deep RL.
question: How do deep RL principles, exploration and spontaneous replay sequences account for decision making in the brain?

name: Wei Pan (Newcastle University)
topics: rl with stability guarantees;meta-rl;multi-robot control;koopman methods
summary: Develops RL and learning-based control methods for robots with stability and safety guarantees.
question: How can Bayesian machine learning and the principles of dynamic control be combined to control robots and multi-robot systems?

name: Applied Computational Psychiatry Lab (Quentin Huys)
topics: computational psychiatry;reinforcement learning;pavlovian bias;dopamine and serotonin;depression
summary: Uses reinforcement-learning models of behaviour to study mechanisms, prediction and treatment of mental illness.
question: How are the brain's computational and learning functions affected in mental illness, and can this understanding yield clinical tools?

name: Barry Lab (Caswell Barry; William de Cothi)
summary: Studies hippocampal and subicular predictive maps related to the successor representation, and replay, using rodent recordings and models.
question: How does the hippocampus learn predictive maps of space and experience, and what substrates support this predictive learning?

name: Jun Wang (UCL Centre for Artificial Intelligence)
topics: multi-agent rl;rl for llm agents;generative decision models;agent memory
summary: Works on multi-agent RL, RL fine-tuning of LLM agents and generative models for decision making.
question: How can multi-agent RL and generative models be combined so that agents learn and adapt from experience?

name: Mirco Musolesi (UCL)
summary: Studies multi-agent RL from a dynamical-systems perspective, distributional RL in chaotic systems and cooperation among LLM agents.
question: How do learning agents, including language-model agents, cooperate and compete in multi-agent systems?

name: Robot Perception and Learning Lab – RPL (Dimitrios Kanoulas)
topics: quadruped loco-manipulation;sim-to-real rl;automated reward design;perceptive locomotion
summary: Develops RL pipelines for legged locomotion and loco-manipulation, including VLM-based automated reward design and sim-to-real deployment.
question: How can articulated robots perceive, decide and control themselves to operate autonomously in unpredictable natural environments?

name: Saxe Lab (Andrew Saxe)
institution: University College London (Gatsby Computational Neuroscience Unit)
topics: learning dynamics theory;rl post-training;deep linear networks;learning in brains
summary: Develops mathematical theory of learning in deep networks and brains, including an analysis of how RL post-training builds compositional reasoning strategies.
question: What mathematical principles describe how learning unfolds in brains and deep neural networks?

name: Özgür Şimşek (University of Bath)
summary: Works on RL foundations including explanations of RL agents with Shapley values and learning distance-based state representations.
question: How can reinforcement-learning agents be understood, explained and made to act well under bounded rationality?

name: Tactile Robotics (Nathan Lepora)
summary: Trains deep RL policies with tactile feedback for dexterous manipulation and sim-to-real transfer.
question: How can robots achieve dexterous manipulation through artificial touch?

name: Prorok Lab (Amanda Prorok)
topics: multi-agent rl;multi-robot systems;behavioural diversity;graph neural networks;multi-agent planning
summary: Develops multi-agent RL and learning-based planning for multi-robot teams, including work on behavioural diversity and intention modelling.
question: How can collective intelligence be built for multi-robot systems?

name: Schultz Lab (Wolfram Schultz)
topics: dopamine;reward prediction error;economic utility;primate neurophysiology;amygdala value coding
summary: Records reward and decision signals in primate dopamine and amygdala neurons and relates them to learning-theory and economic constructs.
question: Which brain signals implement the theoretical constructs underlying reward-seeking, learning and economic choice?

name: Amos Storkey Group (Amos Storkey)
summary: Works on data-efficient and multi-agent RL, including analyses of memory and Markov assumptions in cooperative MARL benchmarks.
question: How can learning systems, including multi-agent RL agents, learn efficiently and continually?

name: Edinburgh Ventures for Intelligence and Economics (Fengxiang He)
summary: Develops learning-theoretic and game-theoretic analyses of RL agents, including safe RL with LTL constraints and generalisation of RLHF.
question: How can the generalisability, rationality and safety of AI agents be understood from learning-theoretic and game-theoretic views?

name: Robust Autonomy and Decisions Group – RAD (Subramanian Ramamoorthy)
primary: robust robot learning and world models
topics: world models;model exploitation;preference learning;manipulation;multi-agent rl benchmarks
summary: Studies learning and adaptation for robots under uncertainty, including world models that RL agents exploit and how to repair them.
question: How can autonomous robots learn and adapt to cope with the uncertain and the unknown?

name: Mingfei Sun (University of Manchester)
topics: policy gradients;multi-agent rl;credit assignment;learning from demonstration
summary: Works on policy-gradient methods, credit assignment in multi-agent RL and learning from demonstration.
question: How can deep RL and learning from demonstration be made efficient for games, robotics and multi-agent systems?

name: Giuseppe De Giacomo (University of Oxford)
summary: Works on LTL/LTLf synthesis and planning, including the use of temporal-logic specifications to structure multi-task RL.
question: How can temporal-logic specifications be used to synthesise and guide the behaviour of agents, including RL agents?

name: Lak Lab (Armin Lak)
topics: dopamine;reward prediction error;decision making;learning trajectories;mouse neurophysiology
summary: Studies how dopamine and striatal circuits implement reward- and sensory-prediction-error learning in mice, linking signals to deep-network and RL models.
question: What neuronal circuit mechanisms underlie learning and decision-making?

name: Neural & Machine Learning Group (Rui Ponte Costa)
summary: Combines neuroscience and machine learning to study learning in the brain, including hippocampal models of multi-task RL under partial observability.
question: What principles underlie learning in the brain?

name: Oxford Control and Verification – OXCAV (Alessandro Abate)
topics: safe rl;formal verification;ltl-guided rl;policy synthesis;stochastic systems
summary: Combines formal verification and control of stochastic systems with RL to synthesise certified policies, including LTL-guided multi-task RL.
question: How can sequential decision making for complex dynamical models, built from first principles or learnt from data, be made safe and certified?

name: Walton Lab (Mark Walton)
topics: dopamine;value learning;reward prediction error;effort-based choice;habit formation
summary: Studies how dopamine and frontal-striatal circuits encode reward, effort and prediction errors during value learning in rodents.
question: How are different aspects of value learned and used to guide decisions, and how does dopamine regulate this moment by moment?

name: Bogacz Group (Rafal Bogacz)
institution: University of Oxford (MRC Brain Network Dynamics Unit)
topics: temporal-difference learning;dopamine;habit formation;action prediction error;basal ganglia
summary: Builds computational models of learning in basal ganglia and cortex, including temporal-difference models of dopamine signals in value learning and habit formation.
question: How do brain networks learn and process information, and how do these dynamics change in neurological disorders?

name: Applied Artificial Intelligence Lab – A2I (Ingmar Posner)
topics: world models;continual learning;off-policy actor-critic;learning from demonstration;robot manipulation
summary: Studies robot learning with world models, off-policy actor-critic methods and learning from demonstration, including benchmarks for continual world-model learning.
question: How can robots that operate in complex real-world settings keep improving through use in their own workspace?

name: Articulated Robotics Group / Dynamic Robot Systems (Ioannis Havoutis)
summary: Trains and deploys RL controllers for quadruped locomotion and loco-manipulation alongside model-based motion optimisation.
question: How can walking robots generate robust, dynamic motion and be deployed in practical field settings?

name: Goal-Oriented Long-Lived Systems – GOALS (Nick Hawes)
topics: risk-aware rl;distributional rl;pomdps;monte carlo tree search;long-term autonomy
summary: Develops planning and RL methods under uncertainty for long-lived mobile robots, including risk-aware and distributional RL and POMDP solvers.
question: How can robots operating for days, weeks or months in dynamic, uncertain environments perform better the longer they act?

name: BOLD Lab – British Open-Ended Learning & Discovery (Jakob Foerster)
lead: Jakob Foerster; Tim Rocktäschel; Laura Toni; Anisoara Calinescu
institution: University of Oxford; University College London; Imperial College London
topics: open-endedness;multi-agent rl;meta-learned rl algorithms;unsupervised environment design;llm agents
summary: Lab formed in 2026 by merging Oxford's FLAIR and WhiRL, UCL's DARK and LASP and Imperial's AIRL groups, working on open-ended learning, multi-agent RL, meta-learned RL algorithms and agent training environments.
question: How can agents keep learning in open-ended environments that supply novel tasks without reliable reward functions, often by creating their own curricula?

name: Bei Peng (University of Sheffield)
summary: Works on deep and multi-agent RL, including safe RL and value estimation with flow matching.
question: How can agents learn to achieve complex goals from experience, with or without interacting with humans?

name: Robert Loftin (University of Sheffield)
topics: ad hoc teamwork;multi-agent rl;human-ai cooperation;safe rl
summary: Applies multi-agent RL to ad hoc collaboration between AI agents and humans.
question: How can AI agents learn to cooperate with new partners, including humans, without prior coordination?

name: Muhammad Burhan Hafez (University of Southampton)
topics: continual learning;intrinsic motivation;world models;robot motor learning
summary: Studies continual robot motor learning with intrinsic motivation, world models and combined model-based and model-free control.
question: How can robots efficiently and continually acquire new skills using intrinsic motivation and adaptive integration of model-based and model-free control?

name: Debmalya Mandal (University of Warwick)
summary: Works on theoretical foundations of RL, including performative RL and corruption-robust RL from human feedback.
question: How should RL algorithms be designed when deployed policies change the environment they learn from?

name: Giovanni Montana (University of Warwick)
summary: Develops offline and offline-to-online RL methods, including for multi-agent settings.
question: How can RL and autonomous decision-making methods be developed from theory to real-world deployment?

name: Long Tran-Thanh (University of Warwick)
summary: Develops online-learning and RL methods with guarantees for systems of collaborating or competing agents.
question: What mathematical foundations allow large systems of autonomous agents to collaborate or act strategically against each other?
